articles.headline: Midseason Metrics Highlight Rockingham Traffic Management
articles.dek: An analytical look at how midpack starters navigated the chaotic Shore Lunch 250 at Rockingham Raceway.
articles.body:
Midpoint of the 20-row calendar brings distinct patterns to light as the series moves away from Rockingham. Eight cautions slowed the Shore Lunch 250 presented by Dutch Boy, creating extended intervals of restart traffic that tested driver patience across the 300-lap distance.

Grid progression metrics from the June 27 short track event show that starting position held less weight than usual for teams who found setup longevity. Tyler Payne advanced 17 spots from eighteenth to capture the checkered flag, pacing the field for 124 laps. Further back, Sean Corr delivered the most notable advancement by climbing 21 positions from twenty-sixth on the grid to finish fifth.

Traffic management remained the defining variable through the middle stints of the race. Drivers who preserved rear tire wear during the eight yellow-flag periods gained significant ground in the final fifty laps, avoiding the attrition that eliminated seven machines before the finish.

Attention now shifts to Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park for the LiUNA! 150 presented by IDEAL Garage Door on July 24. Simulator projections list Brenden Queen as the favorite with seventeen percent win odds, followed by Atsz Minyoung at thirteen percent and Payne at twelve percent as the short track swing continues.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Tyler Payne Charges From 18th to Claim Shore Lunch 250 at Rockingham
articles.dek: Payne led a race-high 124 laps to earn his second victory of the year at the midseason mark.
articles.body:
Tyler Payne carved through the pack from the 18th starting spot at Rockingham Raceway on Tuesday, taking control of the Shore Lunch 250 presented by Dutch Boy and capturing his second win of the season.

Payne paced the field for 124 of the 300 scheduled laps, holding off a late pursuit by Nicholas Hoggeton to cross the line with a 0.593-second advantage. The victory marks Payne's second trip to victory lane through the opening ten rounds of the calendar.

Attrition played a steady role across the afternoon, with eight caution periods slowing the pace and eliminating several contenders. Caleb Guerrier, Willie Mullins, Eric Caudell, and Robbie Kennealy saw their days end early due to accidents. Mechanical troubles struck William Faison and Karson Mitchell with overheating issues, while Ron Vandermeir Jr. dropped out with transmission failure.

Hoggeton started seventh and ran up front for 49 laps before settling for the runner-up position. Points leader Brenden Queen turned a third-place start into a third-place result, leading 31 laps along the way to protect his spot atop the table. Atsz Minyoung also led 31 laps en route to a fourth-place run.

Sean Corr produced the most significant drive through traffic on the afternoon. After rolling off 26th on the grid, Corr worked his way forward, led 25 laps, and took fifth at the checkers. Pole-sitter Vincent Crook led 12 circuits early but slipped back to seventh, just behind Presley Sorah, who controlled 18 laps.

Queen remains out front in the championship with 1,609 points, holding a 120-point cushion over John Verstappen, who finished 12th. Crook sits third with 1,478 points, followed closely by Minyoung at 1,461 and Alfie Denley at 1,448. Payne's second win brings his season total to 1,439 points in sixth position as the series reaches its halfway mark.

The tour now heads into the second half of the 20-race schedule.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

articles.headline: Deep Grid Surges Define Phoenix as Front Row Fades
articles.dek: Heavy attrition and ten cautions opened pathways for drivers starting deep in the field during the General Tire 150.
articles.body:
Passing at Phoenix Raceway usually requires patience, track position, and clean air. The General Tire 150 flipped that expectation across 200 laps, turning the one-mile oval into an afternoon where qualifying near the back proved no barrier to a top-ten result.

While race winner Brenden Queen controlled the front after starting fourth, the running order behind him churned constantly. Ten caution periods interrupted green-flag runs and forced irregular pit strategies. Those stoppages worked directly in favor of several entries that failed to post competitive qualifying times.

## The Climbers Capitalize

Ron Vandermeir Jr. produced the biggest gain of the event. Rolling off in 21st position in the No. 26, Vandermeir avoided seven separate retirements, including accidents that eliminated William Faison and Willie Mullins. Vandermeir picked off positions during restarts, paced the field for nine laps, and crossed the stripe in fourth place.

Vincent Crook executed a similar strategy from 18th on the grid. Crook drove the No. 89 car through traffic, led 11 laps, and finished third. That performance moved him to second in the overall standings with 910 points, sitting 63 markers behind Queen.

Further back, Samuel Riggs advanced 17 spots from his 23rd starting slot to finish sixth, leading seven laps along the way. Even deeper in the order, Alfie Denley climbed from 24th to finish ninth, and Atsz Minyoung took 13th after starting 27th.

## Trouble Near the Front

Starting on the front row offered little protection against the race's chaos. Nicholas Hoggeton qualified second on the outside of row one but failed to lead a single lap, eventually falling backward to finish 12th. Tyler Payne launched from third and remained inside the top ten, but crossed the line in tenth without pacing the field.

Mechanical failures also stripped away prospective contenders. Eric Caudell and Presley Sorah suffered suspension failures, Valdemar Estriden exited with an engine issue, Karson Mitchell retired due to transmission failure, and Ed Pompa dropped out from overheating.

Caleb Costner provided the lone exception among front-runners keeping pace with Queen. Costner started seventh, led 14 laps, and trailed the No. 48 across the line by 0.561 seconds.

With Michigan International Speedway next on the schedule, the series shifts toward high-speed drafting and pure aerodynamic pace. Drivers who survived the chaos at Phoenix will face an entirely different tactical balance on the two-mile oval.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander

articles.headline: Brenden Queen Controls General Tire 150 at Phoenix
articles.dek: Queen led 141 laps from the second row to capture the second race of the ARCA Menards Series season.
articles.body:
AVONDALE, Ariz. — Brenden Queen put on a dominant display at Phoenix Raceway on Sunday, leading 141 of 200 laps to win the General Tire 150. Queen held off a late charge from Caleb Costner, taking the checkered flag with a margin of victory of 0.561 seconds.

Starting from the fourth spot, Queen worked his way to the front and spent the majority of the afternoon controlling the pace out front. The flat one-mile oval produced plenty of chaos behind him, drawing 10 caution flags and sidelining several contenders with mechanical woes and accidents. Neither the restarts nor the traffic disrupted the handling on Queen's No. 48 car.

Costner earned runner-up honors after pacing 14 laps of his own. Vincent Crook climbed from an 18th-place starting spot to round out the podium in third, leading 11 laps during green-flag pit cycles. Ron Vandermeir Jr. earned biggest mover of the race, battling from 21st on the grid to finish fourth and retain the overall lead in the standings.

Daniel Stavchansky rounded out the top five, followed by Samuel Riggs in sixth. Opening-round winner John Verstappen finished seventh after leading six laps. Nick Apollo, Alfie Denley, and Tyler Payne completed the top ten.

Attrition took a heavy toll throughout the 200-lap distance. Seven cars failed to finish, including William Faison and Willie Mullins due to crashes. Eric Caudell and Presley Sorah suffered suspension failures, while engine trouble stopped Valdemar Estriden. Karson Mitchell and Ed Pompa also exited early with transmission and overheating issues, respectively.

Two races into the 20-race schedule, Vandermeir holds the points lead with 340 points, four markers ahead of Verstappen. Queen sits third with 323 points, giving the series two different winners to open the campaign.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Pompa Charges From Rear to Fourth in Daytona Opener
articles.dek: Ed Pompa carved through the Daytona pack from twenty-eighth on the grid to secure a fourth-place finish.
articles.body:
Ed Pompa quietly authored one of the most effective drives of the General Tire 200 at Daytona International Speedway. Starting dead last in twenty-eighth position, the veteran driver methodically worked his way forward through six caution periods over the 188-lap event.

Pompa even found himself at the front of the field for a stretch, leading 18 laps during the superspeedway draft. When the checkered flag waved, he crossed the stripe in fourth place behind race winner John Verstappen, Ron Vandermeir Jr., and Sean Corr.

The massive twenty-four position gain earned Pompa undisputed biggest mover honors for the season opener. It also places him fourth in the early championship standings with 165 points.

Attention now shifts to the flat pavement of Phoenix Raceway for the General Tire 150 on March 5. Pompa will look to carry this early momentum westward.

articles.headline: Verstappen Opens ARCA Season With Daytona Victory
articles.dek: John Verstappen outpaced the field in the General Tire 200, leading 77 laps to kick off the 2028 sim season.
articles.body:
John Verstappen opened the 2028 SIMULATED ARCA Menards Series season with a victory in the General Tire 200 at Daytona International Speedway. Verstappen drove his number 98 machine from the 21st starting spot to lead 77 laps, ultimately securing the win by 1.498 seconds over Ron Vandermeir Jr.

The race featured six cautions and plenty of shuffling through the draft on the superspeedway. Ed Pompa earned biggest mover honors by charging from 28th on the starting grid to finish fourth in the number 10 entry, leading 18 laps along the way.

Ron Vandermeir Jr. finished second after starting fourth and leading 29 laps. Sean Corr crossed the line third after starting 23rd and pacing the field for 19 laps. Nick Apollo rounded out the top five in fifth place after starting 26th and leading 13 laps.

Attrition caught several drivers during the 188-lap opener. Valdemar Estriden exited due to an accident, while McCoy Behnke and Eric Caudell dropped out with overheating issues. Willie Mullins was parked due to damage vehicle policy rules, and Caleb Guerrier was collected in an accident.

Following the opening round, Verstappen sits atop the early championship standings with 185 points. Vandermeir holds second with 175 points, followed by Corr with 170, Pompa with 165, and Apollo with 160.

The ARCA Menards Series continues its 20-race schedule with the next event on the calendar.
articles.author: Ross Delgado

interviews.quote: Starting 26th at this place makes for a lot of work. The car stayed underneath me all afternoon and we took advantage when holes opened up.
We had a solid piece today, just needed a tiny bit more to get to the 79 at the end. Second hurts when you lead laps, but it is good points.
We didn't qualify where we needed to, but the car was dialed in on long runs. Once we got out front in clean air, it was just about hitting marks and managing the gap. Good day for this team.
Starting 21st made our day difficult, but the crew gave me a fast piece. We passed cars all day and kept the points lead.
We had speed, but the 48 was just too strong out in clean air. Second hurts, but we will take the points.
The car was balanced all afternoon. We just stayed out of trouble on the restarts and hit our marks.
We started at the back and just kept digging. Daytona is all about survival and we brought home a solid top five.
The car was hooked up all night. We just had to bide our time and let the draft work for us.

john verstappen.name: John Verstappen
john verstappen.bio: John Verstappen grew up working on dairy equipment in rural Wisconsin before helping his uncle prep street stocks at the local half-mile oval. He spent seven years running regional touring divisions, slowly building a reputation as a clean, low-maintenance driver who rarely tore up equipment. Now piloting the 98 for Shearer Speed Racing, he approaches race weekends with a quiet, blue-collar work ethic.

vincent crook.name: Vincent Crook
vincent crook.bio: Vincent Crook started racing go-karts on temporary asphalt setups in Pacific Northwest industrial parks. After years of self-funding his late model efforts through a commercial plumbing business, he finally caught a break in regional stock car touring series. He brings a gritty, pragmatic approach to the 89 entry for Rise Racing with Earnhardt-Shearer Racing.

kolby newman.name: Kolby Newman
kolby newman.bio: Kolby Newman spent his teens racing dirt modifieds across the Midwest circuits with his father acting as crew chief and engine builder. He transitioned to asphalt via regional developmental combines, showing steady car control on intermediate tracks. Now driving the 99 for Maples Motorsports, he is still learning how to manage full-distance race strategies.

caleb guerrier.name: Caleb Guerrier
caleb guerrier.bio: Caleb Guerrier grew up around swamp buggy races before pivoting to asphalt street stock racing in his early twenties. He bounced through various underfunded independent teams for over a decade, keeping rides afloat with sheer mechanical persistence. Currently piloting the 06 for Wayne Peterson Motorsports, he acts as an on-track veteran who keeps expectations grounded.

tyler payne.name: Tyler Payne
tyler payne.bio: Tyler Payne started in Midwest quarter midgets before moving up through regional asphalt stock car series. He balanced college classes in mechanical engineering with weekend travel to various short tracks across the Great Lakes. Piloting the 79 for ACR Motorsports, he approaches car setups with a technical mindset and calculated execution.

william faison.name: William Faison
william faison.bio: William Faison spent his early years working in coastal boatyards before funding his own hobby stock racing hobby. He spent over a decade quietly climbing the regional ladder without the benefit of major sponsorship backing. Driving the 86 for Clubb Racing Inc., he relies on his extensive endurance racing background to manage worn-out tires.

daniel stavchanksy.name: Daniel Stavchanksy
